scope: FIBA senior men's rules for the global tournaments 2006-2014, each compared with the NBA rule of the same season. Rules are known before a tournament starts, so a tournament reads the period that was in force on its dates.

in_force.source: FIBA rule amendments approved by the Central Board, Beijing, 26 April 2008: https://www.ballineurope.com/the-rules-are-changing/ and https://www.basketballmanitoba.ca/2008/04/fiba-approves-historic-rule-changes.html
in_force.note: The 2010 amendments took effect for Level 1 competitions (Olympics, World Championships) on 1 Oct 2010, after the 2010 World Championship. A 2008 edition of the rules (valid 1 Oct 2008) changed only minor articles (listed under changes_2008).

late_game_timeout_advance.value: After a time-out in the last 2 minutes, the throw-in is taken from the throw-in line in the frontcourt opposite the scorer's table (8.325 m from the endline).

team_foul_penalty.value: A team is in the penalty after 4 team fouls in a period: from the 5th, personal fouls on a player not shooting are 2 free throws. Fouls in an interval count to the next period; all extra-period fouls count as 4th-period fouls (no reset in overtime).
team_foul_penalty.source: FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2014 (approved 2 Feb 2014, valid 1 Oct 2014), copy at https://faculty.kfupm.edu.sa/PE/rabaanha/Official_Basketball_Rules_2014_Y.pdf Art. 41

timeouts.value: 2 in the first half, 3 in the second half, 1 per extra period; unused time-outs do not carry over; 1 minute each
timeouts.source: FIBA Official Basketball Rules Art. 18 as quoted at https://forum.officiating.com/673641-post2.html; FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2014 (approved 2 Feb 2014, valid 1 Oct 2014), copy at https://faculty.kfupm.edu.sa/PE/rabaanha/Official_Basketball_Rules_2014_Y.pdf Art. 18.2
timeouts.note: The 2014 text adds that no more than 2 of the second-half time-outs may be taken in the last 2 minutes; whether that cap existed before the 2014 edition was not established (see research.unresolved).

goaltending_and_interference.value: Goaltending: touching a shot above the ring on its downward flight or after it touched the backboard. Once the ball has touched the ring any player may touch the ball (the restrictions end), but touching the basket or backboard while the ball is on the ring, or a defender touching the ball inside the basket, is interference. From 1 Oct 2008, reaching through the basket from below to touch the ball is interference.
goaltending_and_interference.source: FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2014 (approved 2 Feb 2014, valid 1 Oct 2014), copy at https://faculty.kfupm.edu.sa/PE/rabaanha/Official_Basketball_Rules_2014_Y.pdf Art. 31.2; FIBA rule amendments approved by the Central Board, Beijing, 26 April 2008: https://www.ballineurope.com/the-rules-are-changing/ and https://www.basketballmanitoba.ca/2008/04/fiba-approves-historic-rule-changes.html

goaltending_and_interference.value: Basket interference continues after the ball touches the rim: no player may touch the ball while it is on or directly above the rim (inside the cylinder) - the main contrast with FIBA, where the ball may be played once it touches the ring.
